'''Mark Thomas Vande Hei''' (born November 10, 1966) is a retired [[United States Army]] officer and current [[NASA]] [[astronaut]]<ref name="newclass">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/ascans2009.html|title=NASA Selects New Astronauts for Future Space Exploration|last=NASA HQ|date=June 29, 2009|publisher=[[NASA]]|access-date=June 29, 2009|archive-date=August 1, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090801162824/http://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/ascans2009.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> who has served as a flight engineer for [[Expedition 53]], [[Expedition 54|54]], [[Expedition 64|64]], [[Expedition 65|65]], and [[Expedition 66|66]] on the [[International Space Station]].<ref name =":0">[https://web.archive.org/web/20170908180609/https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-television-coverage-set-for-next-international-space-station-crew-launch-1/ NASA Television Coverage Set for Next International Space Station Crew Launch]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.nasa.gov/spacestation/2018/02/27/touchdown-three-expedition-54-crewmates-back-on-earth/|title=Touchdown! Three Expedition 54 Crewmates Back on Earth – Space Station|website=blogs.nasa.gov|date=February 27, 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=February 28, 2018}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
[[File:Mark Vande Hei talk - NASA logo over Earth.jpg|thumb|Vande Hei giving a talk at the College of St. Benedict / St. John's University in 2012]]

Mark Thomas Vande Hei was born on November 10, 1966, in [[Falls Church, Virginia]] to Dutch parents. He graduated from [[Benilde-St. Margaret's]] High School in [[Saint Louis Park, Minnesota]], in 1985. Vande Hei earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree with a major in [[Physics]] from [[College of Saint Benedict/Saint John's University|Saint John's University]] in 1989, and a [[Master of Science]] degree in [[Applied Physics]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1999.<ref name=nasa_bio>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/astronauts/biographies/mark-t-vande-hei/biography|title=Astronaut Bio: Mark T. Vande Hei |date=April 2021|access-date=July 20, 2021 |publisher=NASA}}</ref>

==Military career==
Vande Hei was commissioned in the U.S. Army through the [[ROTC]] program in 1989 and became a combat engineer, serving in Iraq in [[Operation Provide Comfort]].<ref name=nasa_bio/>  After earning his master's degree in 1999, he became an assistant professor of physics at the [[United States Military Academy]] in West Point. In 2003, he became part of the Army's 1st Space Battalion at [[Peterson Air Force Base]]. Vande Hei again served in Iraq in [[Operation Iraqi Freedom]].<ref name=nasa_bio/> He retired in October 2016 at the rank of [[Colonel (United States)|colonel]].<ref name="retirement">{{cite web|url=https://www.army.mil/article/176526/army_astronaut_retires_after_27_years_of_service|title=Army astronaut retires after 27 years of service|access-date=February 17, 2019|publisher=U.S. Army|date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

==NASA career==
Vande Hei began working at Johnson Space Center in 2006 as part of the U.S. Army contingent there.  He worked as a [[Flight controller#Spacecraft communicator (CAPCOM)|communications officer]] (which is a [[flight controller]]
responsible for communicating with astronauts in space) for the [[International Space Station]]. In June 2009, Vande Hei was selected as a member of the [[NASA Astronaut Group 20]] and he completed astronaut candidate training in June 2011.

On June 10, 2014, NASA announced that Vande Hei would serve as an [[aquanaut]] aboard the [[Aquarius (laboratory)|Aquarius]] [[Underwater habitat|underwater laboratory]] during the [[NEEMO#NEEMO 18: July 21–29, 2014|NEEMO 18]] undersea exploration mission, which began on July 21, 2014, and lasted nine days.<ref name="eighteen">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasa.gov/press/2014/june/nasa-announces-two-upcoming-undersea-missions/#.U6maKldj4jU|title=NASA Announces Two Upcoming Undersea Missions|date=June 10, 2014|publisher=NASA|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref><ref name="Bergin">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2014/06/neemo-returns-two-new-underwater-missions/|title=NEEMO returns with two new underwater missions|last=Bergin|first=Chris|date=June 11, 2014|publisher=[[NASAspaceflight.com|NASASpaceflight]]|access-date=June 24, 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Expedition 49 backup crew members in front of the Soyuz TMA spacecraft mock-up in Star City, Russia.jpg|thumb|Vande Hei, [[Alexander Misurkin]] and [[Nikolai Tikhonov (cosmonaut)|Nikolai Tikhonov]] as part of the [[Soyuz MS-02]] backup crew in [[Star City, Russia]]]]
In May 2015, it was announced that he had been assigned to ISS Expedition 51/52 scheduled to launch in March 2017 aboard [[Soyuz MS-04]]. He was reassigned in November 2016 to ISS Expedition 53/54 scheduled to launch in 2017 aboard [[Soyuz MS-06]].<ref name="exp53">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-updates-2017-international-space-station-crew-assignments|title=NASA Updates 2017 International Space Station Crew Assignments|publisher=NASA|access-date=November 22, 2016|date=November 15, 2016}}</ref>

===Expedition 53/54===
Vande Hei launched to space as part of [[Expedition 53]]/[[Expedition 54|54]] on [[Soyuz MS-06]] on September 12, 2017. After launch the crew performed the fast rendezvous with the ISS and docked automatically after approximately 6 hours.<ref name="launch">{{cite news|last1=Deland|first1=Dave|title=Vande Hei '89 reaches orbit as first Johnnie astronaut|url=http://www.csbsju.edu/news/nasa-launch-2017|access-date=September 27, 2017|publisher=College of St. Benedict / St. John's University|date=September 13, 2017}}</ref>

On October 5, 2017, Vande Hei performed his first spacewalk, along with commander [[Randolph Bresnik|Randy Bresnik]]. The spacewalk replaced the gripping mechanism on [[Canadarm2]], the latching end effector A, or LEE-A. The duration was 6 hours and 55 minutes.<ref name="EVA1">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spacewalk-aging-robot-arm-requires-surgery/ |title=Aging robot arm gets spacewalk surgery |last=Harwood |first=William |date=October 5, 2017 |access-date=October 5, 2017 |publisher=cbsnews}}</ref> On October 10, 2017, they completed the second EVA of the mission. They lubricated the newly installed end effector and replaced cameras, and the duration was 6 hours and 26 minutes.

The expedition ended on February 27, 2018, at 9:31&nbsp;p.m. EST with Vande Hei's, Bresnik's, and third crew member [[Joseph M. Acaba]]'s successful landing back on Earth.<ref name=":0" />

===Expedition 64/65/66===
[[File:Expedition 65 crew greeting.jpg|thumb|Mark’s arrival during Expedition 64]]
In March 2021 it was confirmed that Vande Hei would be making a second spaceflight, as a flight engineer onboard [[Soyuz MS-18]], and be part of ISS [[Expedition 64]]/[[Expedition 65|65]].<ref name="ms-18_assign">{{cite web
  | last1 = Scierholz
  | first1 = Stephanie
  | last2 = Sumner
  | first2 = Megan
  | last3 = Ballarte
  | first3 = Chelsea
  | title = NASA Assigns Astronaut Mark Vande Hei to International Space Station Crew
  | publisher = NASA
  | date = March 9, 2021
  | url = https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-assigns-astronaut-mark-vande-hei-to-international-space-station-crew
  | accessdate = April 9, 2021 }}</ref><ref name="exp-64-65">{{cite web
  | last = Garcia
  | first = Mike
  | title = NASA TV Broadcasts Friday Launch to Station on Soyuz Crew Ship
  | publisher = NASA
  | date = April 8, 2021
  | url = https://blogs.nasa.gov/spacestation/2021/04/08/nasa-tv-broadcasts-friday-launch-to-station-on-soyuz-crew-ship/
  | accessdate = April 9, 2021 }}</ref> On April 9, 2021, Vande Hei alongside [[Roscosmos]] cosmonauts [[Oleg Novitsky]] and [[Pyotr Dubrov]] successfully launched onboard [[Soyuz MS-18]] at 3:42{{nbsp}}am EDT.<ref name="ms-18_launch">{{cite web
  | last = Garcia
  | first = Mike
  | title = Station Crew Blasts Off on Short Ride to Station
  | publisher = NASA
  | date = April 9, 2021
  | url = https://blogs.nasa.gov/spacestation/2021/04/09/station-crew-blasts-off-on-short-ride-to-station/
  | accessdate = April 9, 2021 }}</ref>
[[File:Expedition 65 inflight crew portrait (1).jpg|thumb|Mark during Expedition 65 playing Space Olympics]]
On September 14, 2021, it was announced that Vande Hei and [[Pyotr Dubrov]] had their six-month stays on the station extended by another six months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spacenews.com/nasa-astronaut-to-stay-on-iss-for-nearly-a-year|title=NASA astronaut to stay on ISS for nearly a year|date=September 14, 2021|accessdate=September 26, 2021}}</ref> This means Vande Hei broke the [[List of spaceflight records#Ten longest human spaceflights|record for the longest spaceflight]] by an American astronaut with 355 days. Later, [[Francisco Rubio (astronaut)|Francisco Rubio]] broke his record with a total of 371 days in September 2023.<ref name="nasa-20230912">{{cite web |last1=Cranford |first1=Nathan |title=Astronaut's Record-Setting Mission Helps NASA Plan Deep Space Journeys |url=https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/astronauts-record-setting-mission-helps-nasa-plan-deep-space-journeys/ |publisher=[[NASA]] |access-date=4 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230930161914/https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/astronauts-record-setting-mission-helps-nasa-plan-deep-space-journeys/ |archive-date=30 September 2023 |date=12 September 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Two weeks of technical and weather delays, together with Crew-2 approaching the maximum on-orbit duration of their Crew Dragon craft, forced a highly undesirable “indirect handover”. As such, Crew-2 departed the station on November 8, 2021, whilst Crew-3 launched three days later and arrived safely at the sprawling orbital outpost on November 11, 2021. In this instance, there was no absence of U.S. personnel since NASA’s Mark Vande Hei was still on ISS. But had he not been aboard, the indirect handover of USOS operations from Crew-2 to Crew-3 might have left an unwanted gap in U.S. station crewing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2022 |title=Rubio Primed for Integrated Crew Ops, Cristoforetti, Prokopyev to Command Expedition 68a/b - AmericaSpace |url=https://www.americaspace.com/2022/08/23/rubio-primed-for-integrated-crew-ops-cristoforetti-prokopyev-to-command-expedition-68/ |access-date=September 23, 2022 |website=www.americaspace.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

On January 6, 2022, Hei and Dubrov completed 273 days on ISS, surpassing [[Andrew R. Morgan]]‘s record of 272 days on-board.<ref>{{Cite web|last=NASA|date=January 6, 2022|title=Biology and Agriculture Research on Space Station As Astronaut Begins Record-Breaking Spree|url=https://scitechdaily.com/?p=149025|access-date=January 7, 2022|website=SciTechDaily|language=en-US}}</ref> Shortly before his return to Earth, he passed 340 days in space, surpassing [[Scott Kelly (astronaut)|Scott Kelly]] as the record holder for the longest American spaceflight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/feature/record-breaking-nasa-astronaut-mark-vande-heis-contributions-to-human-research-studies/|title = Mark Vande Hei's Contributions to Human Research Studies|date = March 14, 2022}}</ref>
[[File:ISS-66 Astronaut Mark Vande Hei harvests plants grown on petri plates.jpg|thumb|Astronaut Mark Vande Hei harvests plants grown on petri plates during Expedition 66]]
He returned to Earth with [[Soyuz MS-19]] on March 30, 2022, having spent a total of 355 days in space on a mission to better observe the effects of long-duration spaceflight on humans.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=NASA Astronaut to Discuss American Space Record in News Conference |url=https://www.nasa.gov/press-release/nasa-astronaut-to-discuss-american-space-record-in-news-conference |website=NASA.gov|date=April 2022 }}</ref>
[[File:Expedition 66 Soyuz Landing (NHQ202203300002).jpg|thumb|Mark on Soyuz MS-19 landing]]

====Return====
On March 10, 2022, [[Dmitry Rogozin]] posted a video on social media threatening to abandon Vande Hei on the ISS in retaliation against American sanctions on Russia's [[high tech]] imports that were placed upon [[Russia]] after [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|the Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abc7ny.com/russia-international-space-station-mark-vande-hei-iss-american-astronaut/11639556/|title = Russia threatens to abandon American astronaut in space as sanctions threaten peace aboard ISS|date = March 10, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 11, 2022 |title=Twin Cities astronaut facing threats from Russian Space Agency |url=https://www.kare11.com/article/news/nation-world/ukraine/twin-cities-astronaut-mark-vande-hei-facing-threats-from-russian-space-agency/89-7f893171-c2e1-4009-81e6-ad65d3b21011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220330132422/https://www.kare11.com/article/news/nation-world/ukraine/twin-cities-astronaut-mark-vande-hei-facing-threats-from-russian-space-agency/89-7f893171-c2e1-4009-81e6-ad65d3b21011 |archive-date=March 30, 2022 |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=[[KARE (TV)]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He landed as planned on March 30.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Davenport |first=Christian |date=March 30, 2022 |title=NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei, Russian cosmonauts return safely to Earth |language=en-US |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2022/03/30/mark-vande-hei-return/ |access-date=March 30, 2022 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

Six months after returning from his 355 days in space, Mark returned to his high school, Benilde-St. Margaret's on September 23, 2022. During the 2015-2016 school year, two students from Benilde-St. Margaret's were chosen to give their student ID cards to Vande Hei so he could take the cards to space with him. Mark returned these IDs when at the school.<ref>{{cite web |title=Benilde-St. Margaret's welcomes back NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei for homecoming |url=https://www.startribune.com/benilde-st-margarets-welcomes-back-nasa-astronaut-mark-vande-hei-for-homecoming/600209664/ |website=[[Star Tribune]]|date=September 23, 2022 }}</ref> A representative for Minnesota Governor [[Tim Walz]] declared September 23, 2022 to be Mark Vande Hei Day in Minnesota. Brian Bruess, the president of the [[College of Saint Benedict and Saint John's University]], also came to congratulate Vande Hei.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 September 2022 |title=Astronaut Mark Vande Hei Honored by BSM Community |url=https://www.bsmschool.org/who-we-are/news/news-details/~board/all-bsm-news/post/astronaut-mark-vande-hei-honored-by-bsm-community |access-date=20 November 2022 |website=[[Benilde-St. Margaret's]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He was born in Virginia and raised in New Jersey and Minnesota. He is married to Julie Vande Hei and has two children.<ref name=nasa_bio />

==Cinematography==
On May 14, 2021, the Interagency Committee approved the composition of the ISS main and alternate crews for the period 2021-2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Космонавты готовятся к очередной экспедиции на МКС |url=https://www.gctc.ru/main.php?id=5326 |website=Новости |publisher=[[Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330110929/https://www.gctc.ru/main.php?id=5326 |archive-date=March 30, 2022 |language=ru |date=May 25, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cosmonaut Anton Shkaplerov (commander) and the crew of the film ''[[The Challenge (2022 film)|The Challenge]]'': actress [[Yulia Peresild]] and director [[Klim Shipenko]] went to the ISS onboard Soyuz MS-19. The drama is a joint project of [[Roscosmos]], [[Channel One Russia|Channel One]] and the [[Yellow, Black and White]] studio.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url= https://tass.ru/kosmos/11279593|title=Актриса и режиссер фильма "Вызов" полетят к МКС 5 октября |language=ru |website= |publisher= [[ТАСС]]|date= April 29, 2021|access-date=April 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Экспедиция МКС-65/66. План полёта|url= https://www.roscosmos.ru/30919/ |language=ru |work=[[Русский космос (журнал)|Русский космос]] |date=April 2021 |page=17}}</ref>

The director and actress returned to Earth on October 17, 2021 on Soyuz MS-18 with commander Oleg Novitskiy. Pyotr Dubrov and Mark Vande Hei, who arrived at the ISS on Soyuz MS-18, joined Shkaplerov on the landing of Soyuz MS-19 on March 30, 2022.<ref name="tass 2021-03-14">{{cite web |url=https://tass.ru/kosmos/10899815 |title=Срок полета двух членов экипажа "Союза МС-18" увеличат |language=ru |website=[[ТАСС]] |date=March 14, 2021 |access-date=April 23, 2021}}</ref><ref name="rc 2021-04-09">{{cite web |url=https://www.roscosmos.ru/30638/ |title=На МКС 10 человек |website=[[Роскосмос]] |date=April 9, 2021 |access-date=April 30, 2021|language=ru}}</ref>

Klim Shipenko shot about 35–40 minutes of film on the ISS, as well as taking on the position of director, operator, art director, and makeup artist. Oleg Novitsky and Pyotr Dubrov will appear in the film,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.roscosmos.ru/32044/|title=Создатели научно-просветительского проекта "Вызов" раскрыли некоторые секреты фильма|date=July 31, 2021|accessdate=August 7, 2021|language=ru}}</ref> with Dubrov and Mark Vande Hei assisting in the production.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tass.com/science/1303107|title=Russia to switch to year-long expeditions to orbital outpost, says Roscosmos chief | date=June 16, 2021|accessdate=July 12, 2021}}</ref>
